$schema: none — hand-maintained; every number below was MEASURED, never copied from a plan

recordedFrom.note: Values produced by `node scripts/sec-selftest.mjs` on a clean tree at the commit this file landed in. They are OBSERVATIONS, not targets: nothing here was transcribed from a design document. Re-record deliberately (run the selftest, read the diff, justify every moved number in the PR) — never regenerate it to make a red build green.

optionalGatesNote: Gates listed here may come back `unmeasured` without failing the build. They are still NOT counted as passes: the run reports them as UNMEASURED and `verdict.allGatesPassed` goes false. Only recheck qualifies, because it ships a JVM jar that is installed with `npm install --no-save recheck` and is therefore absent on a default CI runner (sec-a1-catalog.mjs header). Everything else that cannot be measured is a failure.

corpus:samples/safe._why: E3. The false-positive contract: correct code must produce nothing. Pinned as a multiset of ruleId@file rather than as `length === 0` so the failure names the rule that started firing.
corpus:samples/safe._filesWhy: Directory census, checked BEFORE the finding snapshot. Without it an emptied or renamed fixture set makes the [] snapshot of a false-positive corpus compare equal and pass, reporting that the zero-false-positive contract holds having scanned nothing. Same argument as b1/b3 corpus-scale.

corpus:samples/vulnerable._why: E2 = 51 findings. The scalar 51 is the number everyone quotes; the SET is what a regression actually moves. A rule that stops firing while another starts leaves 51 intact.

a1:surface-census._why: The ReDoS attack surface, counted. A new rule adds patterns; this is what makes that visible the day it lands rather than the day someone writes an attack string for it.
a1:surface-census._rebaselined: 0.3.0-beta: 71 rules / 127 patterns -> 72 / 137. VG-AISC-004 (Mock/Dummy Security Leftover) landed in packages/rules and brought 10 patterns with it. The gate fired, which is it working; the number was only moved after the surface it counts was measured, not because the count was inconvenient. Evidence gathered before this edit: (1) a1:shape-suspicious-set PASSES, so none of the 10 has a superlinear-prone shape; (2) a1:catalog-errors and a1:unreached-literals both PASS; (3) the real product path was timed against seven adversarial inputs of 30-60k characters chosen to stress this rule's own vocabulary (long space/word/brace/paren runs after a mock-ish prefix, and 3,000 repetitions of a mock-auth function) and the WORST full scan was 41 ms against a 3,000 ms D3 contract. The timing harness carried a positive control (a hard-coded AWS key returning VG-SEC-001, and mockAuthenticate returning VG-AISC-004) because a harness that finds nothing measures nothing - an earlier version of this probe read the wrong field, reported 0 patterns, and would have declared PASS having tested nothing at all.
a1:surface-census._measuredNote: rulesWithPatterns === totalRules is load-bearing: sec-a1-catalog.mjs found that a source-literal scan misses VG-CRYPTO-002 (it builds its patterns with `new RegExp(...)`), so the catalogue hooks RegExp.prototype.exec instead. A rule that stops reporting patterns would shrink the surface silently.

a1:shape-suspicious-set._why: §9.4「新ルールで super-linear が混入したら fail」. Grain is (ruleId, patternIndex, hit-ids): the catalogue summary reports 4 suspicious RULES but those rules carry 7 suspicious PATTERNS (VG-QUAL-007 alone has three), so a rule-count pin would miss an eighth added to an already-suspicious rule.
a1:shape-suspicious-set._measuredNote: These 7 are the residue of the L1 rewrite, all `adjacent-unbounded` except VG-QUAL-001#0. They are heuristic hits, NOT proven super-linear: the wall-clock property is asserted separately by packages/analyzer-core/src/redos-invariant.test.ts. This gate pins the SHAPE census, not safety.

a1:unreached-literals._why: Source literals the runtime hook never executed on the probe. They still run on real input, so they are attack surface the n–T harness cannot reach; growth of this multiset must be a deliberate edit.

a1:catalog-errors._why: A rule that throws on the probe, or a pattern that does not compile, silently shrinks the measured surface and flatters every A1 number.

a1:crossfile-surface-census._why: The OTHER half of the regex attack surface: packages/analysis-graph, the cross-file design-smell layer that ships in the CLI and the Action. sec-a1-catalog.mjs loads packages/rules ONLY, so until this gate existed a super-linear pattern added to a cross-file rule passed all nineteen gates (MEASURED LIMIT 8). Pinned on the STATIC axis — regex literals and `new RegExp(` construction sites in the built package — because that is a function of the build alone.
a1:crossfile-surface-census._whyNotOneCensusWithA1SurfaceCensus: A core rule's pattern set is fixed by the build: one inert probe string reaches every pattern and the count cannot move without a source change. A cross-file rule builds patterns FROM ITS INPUT (`new RegExp(String.raw`\b${escaped}\b`)` over identifiers read out of the analysed file), so the number of patterns it executes is a function of the FIXTURE TREE, not of the build. MEASURED: 332 (rule, pattern) pairs over the 130 fixture projects present in the working tree that recorded this, and 270 over the 86 that were tracked in git at that moment. An exact pin on that number fails whenever a fixture lands, and a gate people re-record without reading is worse than no gate.
a1:crossfile-surface-census._measuredCoverage: 23 built .js files (test bundles excluded), 194 regex literals of which 124 are in design-smells-crossfile/, and 24 `new RegExp(` sites. Cross-check against the runtime arm: 101 of the patterns that actually executed appear in NO source literal (they are constructed), which is the VG-CRYPTO-002 lesson reproduced in this layer and the reason the static count alone is not called coverage.

a1:crossfile-shape-suspicious-set._why: §9.4「新ルールで super-linear が混入したら fail」 for the cross-file layer, over BOTH arms: the regex literals found statically in the built package, and the fully-resolved patterns captured at runtime (interpolation already applied, so an `(a+)+` assembled from a template is visible here and nowhere else).
a1:crossfile-shape-suspicious-set._measuredNote: EMPTY, measured over 194 static literals and 332 runtime (rule, pattern) pairs with the same three shape checks sec-a1-catalog.mjs uses. Empty is also the one value that is stable across fixture sets: the runtime pattern population of any subset of the fixture tree is a subset of the population measured here, so an empty set on a dirty working tree stays empty on a CI checkout with fewer fixtures. As in a1:shape-suspicious-set this pins the SHAPE census, not safety — it is a heuristic, and no recheck/automaton oracle is wired into the cross-file script.

a1:crossfile-probe-liveness._why: The anti-vacuity half. `0 patterns observed` and `no super-linear pattern observed` are the same JSON, and this repo has produced both accidents already — a corpus gate that passed with its fixtures deleted, and an A1 timing probe that read the wrong field, measured 0 patterns and declared PASS. The positive control is the exact part: four named product regexes must have executed. Three of them (authzComparisonPattern / authzFlagPattern / authzMembershipPattern) are built with `new RegExp(String.raw...)` and are invisible to any source-literal scan, so they only appear if the runtime hook genuinely ran; TEST_PATH is a plain literal, so a failure distinguishes 'the hook is broken' from 'the driver reached no rule at all'.
a1:crossfile-probe-liveness._whyFloorsNotPins: The driver is samples/crossfile-fixtures, whose size differs between a working tree and a fresh checkout (130 vs 86 fixture projects when this was recorded — 44 of the 0.3.0-β fixture directories were still untracked). The floors are set well under the TRACKED-only measurement (270 pairs / 86 projects / 75 runtime-only patterns) so a CI checkout passes, and the sharp checks are the exact ones beside them.

a1:recheck-superlinear._why: The automaton oracle. OPTIONAL and recorded here as UNMEASURED: recheck is not a devDependency (JVM jar, `npm install --no-save recheck`), so on CI it is absent and this gate reports `unmeasured`. It is never a pass.
a1:recheck-superlinear.reason: recheck is not installed in CI; sec-a1-catalog.mjs reports recheck.available=false and falls back to the shape heuristic only

b1:corpus-scale._why: The vacuous-pass guard. A generator that silently degrades emits a tiny corpus, ER lands at 0.0, and the ceiling gate goes green over nothing. Pinned EXACTLY (not as a floor) because a floor still allows one transform to stop applying while another compensates. corpusFiles is read back off disk, so a manifest that claims 416 pairs while 3 files landed is caught too.

b1:er-true-ceiling._why: ER of the SHIPPED engine (canonicalize:true) on the headline basis the evaluator designates: matched pairs, one shared denominator, `exists` observation, negative controls excluded. Higher = an attacker can rewrite more real findings away.

b1:er-false-ceiling._why: ER of the pre-D2 CONTROL arm. Gated too, because ΔER is only interpretable if the control holds still: a drifting control can make D2 look better or worse without D2 changing at all.

b1:delta-er-floor._why: ΔER = ER(pre-D2) − ER(shipped): the share of evasion the D2 canonicalization pre-pass absorbs. This is the gate that catches D2 being disabled — that leaves both arms equal and BOTH ceilings satisfied.

b1:harness-integrity._why: MEASURED: sec-b1-er-eval.mjs exits 0 even when its own rescan assertions are BROKEN (its tail writes the JSON and prints "⚠ BROKEN" with no process.exit). Gating on the child exit code alone is therefore a vacuous pass, so the verdict is read out of the JSON. NC2 is the noop transform: any evasion it shows means the harness fabricates concealment, which would invalidate every ER number above it.

b3:corpus-scale._why: Same vacuous-pass hazard as B1: an empty disguise corpus makes CR 0 and every ceiling green.

b3:cr-gated-ceiling._why: CR after D1, at the WORST-CASE (transform, severity) row — never a pooled mean, for the reason sec-b3-cr-eval.mjs gives: an attack that works on one row is not diluted by the rows it does not touch. The row identity is pinned too, so the threshold cannot silently start describing a different attack.

b3:d1-reduction-floor._why: CR_ungated − CR_gated at the same worst-case row: how much concealment the D1 severity floor removes. This is the quantity with a genuine LOWER bound. Reading 「CR が baseline 下限を割ったら fail」 as "gated CR must not fall" would be backwards — a falling CR is the defence working. Removing D1 does not push CR above a ceiling it was already under; it collapses this reduction.

b3:undeclared-cr-ceiling._why: D1's declared defence target: a disguise the attacker never declares must be worth nothing after the severity floor. DECLARED suppression is a legitimate product feature (its CR is 0.5 and is deliberately NOT gated to 0) — gating the pooled number would have forced that feature to look like a vulnerability.

b3:harness-integrity._why: sideConstraintsAllOk is a genuine CROSS-CHECK, not a duplicate of the corpus arm: sec-b3-cr-eval.mjs reaches the rule layer directly (allRules + explainContextConfidence) while the corpus arm goes through scanPath. Two independent paths agreeing on samples/safe=0 and samples/vulnerable=51 is worth more than either alone, and a disagreement between them would itself be the finding. pairingAgreement is a FLOOR (a re-derived SCOPE §2.1 pairing that agrees less often means the manifest and the evaluator are drifting).
